title.narrative: Rohingya Crisis Appeal - End of Appeal Evaluation

description.narrative:
In August 2017 a violent crackdown by Myanmar’s military on Rohingya people living primarily in Rakhine State in Myanmar led to hundreds of thousands of Rohingya fleeing the violence in which over 6,700 were killed, thousands were injured including through rape and other forms of sexual abuse. Many of their homes and villages were destroyed. Over 700,000 sought refuge in the Cox’s Bazaar area of Bangladesh. The Rohingya have endured decades of persecution & displacement, with over 100,000 Rohingya refugees already living in Bangladesh, primarily in the Cox’s Bazaar region prior to the August 2017 influx.
CAFOD responded with support to two long-term CAFOD partners, Caritas Bangladesh and DAM, who were involved in the immediate, community-led response where local communities provided emergency relief such as food & shelter. A large-scale response was rapidly established with significant presence of UN agencies, international NGOs as well as Bangladesh national NGOs with significant experience of emergency response.
This evaluation aims to draw together learning from across CAFOD’s Rohingya Crisis response to understand how best we can strategically support responses that align with & support our strategic priorities. A short evaluation report including evaluation findings, lessons learnt & recommendations for action will be the key output of the evaluation. This project will cover the costs of an experienced consultant with expertise to undertake the evaluation & work with partners and CAFOD staff to produce a high quality final report.
